key_insight: A flexible foil elastically mounted at the leading edge can achieve better self-propulsion when passive heave and deformation are allowed, revealing an additional optimal regime near the translational spring resonance beyond the classic torsional resonance.
engineering_relevance: Designing flapping or bio-inspired propulsion systems should consider both spring tuning and foil flexibility, since lower stiffness can shift the best efficiency toward a distinct, higher-performing operating branch.
method: Small-amplitude analytical fluid-structure interaction model for an elastically mounted flexible foil
Leading edge driven by an oscillating force, enabling passive heave, pitch, and deformation
Model validated against prior theoretical and experimental rigid-plate results
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparison with previous theoretical and experimental results and identifies two local optima in stride length and efficiency across spring-stiffness ranges.
watch_item: The formulation is small-amplitude, so the predicted optima may not fully extend to strongly nonlinear flapping or large-deformation regimes.
paper_title: Aquatic locomotion by an elastically mounted flexible foil actuated by an oscillating force
